positions.summary_short: Heidi Lorenz seeks re-election to build on four years of progress, citing the Health Hub, downtown foundation and transit investment.
summary_bullets: Incumbent mayor of four years, 16 years total municipal service (Ward Councillor, District Councillor, then Mayor).
Cites successes: residential development attracted, expanded transportation services, and the upcoming Gravenhurst Health Hub opening; business investment on Winhara Rd, Bethune Drive and Highway 11.
Says council accountability, transparency and improved communication were promises made and kept; the foundation for a vibrant downtown is laid.
Points to the return of Ontario Northland train service as more good things to come.
positions.verbatim_quote: Council accountability, transparency and improved communication were promises made and kept. The foundation for a vibrant downtown has been laid, we can't stop now.
positions.source_title: Candidate Profiles - Town of Gravenhurst official election page

positions.summary_short: Jo Morphy wants a full-service South Muskoka hospital with at least 60 beds and local obstetrics, and rejects the transfer model.
summary_bullets: Wants a full-service hospital, not a smaller one, while the population is growing; supports a minimum of 60 acute-care beds.
Opposes the transfer model: once she arrives at her local hospital the only acceptable transfer is for immediate specialized care.
Supports maintaining fully functioning obstetrics in South Muskoka.
Would not commit municipal taxpayer funding to a plan that leaves South Muskoka behind.
Does not support the current MAHC redevelopment model as equitable for South Muskoka residents.
positions.verbatim_quote: I do not like the transfer model. I dislike the idea that I have to triage whatever situation I am dealing with before deciding to go to Bracebridge or Orillia because I do not want to end up as far away as Huntsville.
positions.source_title: SSMHC 2026 Municipal Candidate Questionnaire Results - Gravenhurst

positions.summary_short: Jo Morphy pledges accountable leadership, stewardship of resources and protection of the lakes.
summary_bullets: Twice-elected Town Councillor and past president of the Muskoka Bay Property Owners Association, nearly a decade of service.
Business background with an analytical mind; emphasizes strong regional relationships.
Cares deeply about the lakes and their ecosystems; protecting the lakes means protecting the Town.
positions.verbatim_quote: Jo cares deeply about the lakes and their ecosystems, and knows that protecting the lakes means protecting the Town.
positions.source_title: Candidate Profiles - Town of Gravenhurst official election page

positions.summary_short: Jeff Watson promises listening-first leadership, solid municipal services and careful budgeting.
summary_bullets: Pledges to be accessible, listen carefully and give residents meaningful opportunities to share views.
Will focus on maintaining roads, parks, facilities and municipal services, improving service delivery and doing the basics well.
Every dollar comes from taxpayers: supports careful budgeting, practical choices and long-term planning that delivers real value.
Will work with the business community to address challenges and barriers.
positions.verbatim_quote: Every dollar the Town spends comes from the people it serves. I'll support careful budgeting, practical choices and long-term planning that delivers real value.
positions.source_title: Watson for Mayor of Gravenhurst - campaign website

positions.summary_short: Marc Mantha backs at least 60 beds and local maternity care, and ties municipal funding to a plan that meets future demand.
summary_bullets: Supports a minimum of 60 acute-care beds, believing population growth may exceed forecasts and infrastructure must be planned ahead.
Says the Pine Street site information exists but must be made accessible in plain language; believes MAHC adequately demonstrated the site.
Will only commit municipal taxpayer funding once satisfied the final plan provides adequate and equitable capacity for South Muskoka.
Wants maternity care close to home wherever clinically appropriate; opposes routine transfers due to South Muskoka capacity limits.
Undecided on the current model; wants important questions answered and adequacy measured against growth, aging and seasonal demand.
positions.verbatim_quote: Healthcare infrastructure is too important to size only for today's needs. I support advocating for a minimum of 60 acute-care beds at the future South Muskoka hospital, while continuing to assess what will be required as our population and healthcare needs evolve.
positions.source_title: SSMHC 2026 Municipal Candidate Questionnaire Results - Gravenhurst

positions.summary_short: Marc Mantha promises tax stewardship, bold housing action, health care for all and protection of Gravenhurst's character.
summary_bullets: Says growth brings opportunity and responsibility: excellence in municipal service, strong tax stewardship, thoughtful planning, infrastructure investment.
Promises a bold approach to housing, economic opportunity, and primary healthcare for all.
Wants to protect the character and natural beauty that make Gravenhurst special.
positions.verbatim_quote: Gravenhurst is growing, and with growth comes both opportunity and responsibility: excellence in municipal service, strong tax stewardship, thoughtful planning, infrastructure investment, a bold approach to housing, economic opportunity, and primary healthcare for all, while protecting the character and natural beauty that make this town so special.
positions.source_title: Candidate Profiles - Town of Gravenhurst official election page

positions.summary_short: Penny Varney is running for District Council on waste, taxes, environmental sustainability and housing.
summary_bullets: Ward 1 Councillor for the past 8 years; 45-year Gravenhurst resident; business owner (jewellery gallery and pharmacy).
Top criteria: waste management, property taxes, and environmental sustainability; at the very top is housing and the cost of houses.
Says many of these are dealt with at the District level, which is why she is running for District Council.
positions.verbatim_quote: Waste management, property taxes, and environmental sustainability are top criteria. Of course at the very top is housing and the cost of houses.
positions.source_title: Candidate Profiles - Town of Gravenhurst official election page

positions.summary_short: Jaden Hollingshead prioritizes affordable housing, a year-round downtown and environmental protection.
summary_bullets: Executive Director of the Bracebridge Chamber of Commerce for three years; sits on the board of the Muskoka Community Land Trust.
Priorities: housing that people who work here can actually afford, a vibrant year-round downtown, protecting lakes and forests.
Wants Gravenhurst's voice to carry weight at both Town and District tables; believes government works best when residents see what and why something is decided.
positions.verbatim_quote: His priorities are housing that people who work here can actually afford, a vibrant downtown that stays busy year-round, protecting the lakes and forests that make this place what it is.
positions.source_title: Candidate Profiles - Town of Gravenhurst official election page

positions.summary_short: Christina Hunter wants local obstetrics, ALC beds in seniors homes, and a final plan addressing both before funding.
summary_bullets: Supports obstetrics staying in South Muskoka; driving to Huntsville from remote areas equals driving to Barrie, too far for maternity care.
Says common services should stay at both hospitals to limit transfers, without duplicating specialized services.
Favors adding ALC beds in seniors care homes like the Pines, Alexander and Muskoka Shores to relieve hospital beds.
Before endorsing a plan with funding attached she needs a final plan addressing the ALC plan and obstetrics.
positions.verbatim_quote: As mentioned previously, driving to Huntsville for obstetrics for someone living in remote areas of South Muskoka would be the equivalent of driving to Barrie, which is too far for obstetrics care.
positions.source_title: SSMHC 2026 Municipal Candidate Questionnaire Results - Gravenhurst

positions.summary_short: Christina Hunter campaigns on waste diversion and housing for those in deepest need.
summary_bullets: Current Ward 5 Councillor and Alternate District Councillor; enjoyed her first term working directly with residents.
Passionate about waste diversion strategies and housing initiatives for those in the deepest need.
Seeks District Council vote to continue moving the dial on these issues.
positions.verbatim_quote: I'm passionate about waste diversion strategies and housing initiatives for those in the deepest need.
positions.source_title: Candidate Profiles - Town of Gravenhurst official election page

positions.summary_short: Erin Strength supports the MAHC redevelopment model, fearing opposition risks losing the hospital, and backs the Pine Street site.
summary_bullets: Happy to advocate for 60 beds as a starting point, understanding the plan starts at 46 and can expand.
Supports the current MAHC redevelopment model; fears fighting the proposal risks losing the new hospital entirely.
Says obstetrics absence would not break her support; hopes the Gravenhurst Health Hub could accommodate obstetrics services.
Supports the Pine Street site (closer than Royal Muskoka site for constituents) and Gravenhurst's municipal hospital share.
Wants transparency: uneasy about behind-closed-doors hospital discussions.
positions.verbatim_quote: Once again, I am worried that if we continue to fight against the proposal that we have that we won't get anything.
positions.source_title: SSMHC 2026 Municipal Candidate Questionnaire Results - Gravenhurst

positions.summary_short: Erin Strength runs on affordable housing, the Health Hub, low tax levies and waste initiatives.
summary_bullets: Incumbent Ward Councillor (2014) and District Councillor (2022); full-time Gravenhurst resident since age 7.
Proponent of affordable housing on First St and Pine St; steady advocate of the Gravenhurst Health Hub and the Fire Department ladder truck.
Supported one of the lowest tax levy increases in Muskoka four years running; backed clear bags and garbage/recycling initiatives extending landfill life.
positions.verbatim_quote: Erin was a proponent of affordable housing on First St and Pine St in Bracebridge. She has been a steady advocate of the Gravenhurst Health Hub.
positions.source_title: Candidate Profiles - Town of Gravenhurst official election page

positions.summary_short: Sandy Cairns fights for equal rights at the South Muskoka hospital and warns against forcing births and stroke care to Huntsville.
summary_bullets: Unable to complete the full questionnaire due to personal circumstances; provided a statement by email.
Says South Muskoka hospital must have equal rights and opportunities; the hospital will only get busier.
Calls driving to Huntsville for a baby or stroke care a potential life-and-death circumstance, which she says is wrong.
Notes no beds now, people in hallways, and her own mother waiting in emerg overnight for admission.
positions.verbatim_quote: Drive in either by car or ambulance up the highway to have a baby or to get stroke care may be a life and death circumstance and that is so wrong !!
positions.source_title: SSMHC 2026 Municipal Candidate Questionnaire Results - Gravenhurst

positions.summary_short: Sandy Cairns campaigns on moving the Gravenhurst Health Hub forward and protecting the environment.
summary_bullets: More than 26 years of municipal service, multiple terms as Gravenhurst Councillor and District Councillor.
Serves on the Health Services Committee and Simcoe Muskoka District Health Unit as Vice Chair.
Mission has been to actively move the Gravenhurst Health Hub forward; focused on initiatives that protect the environment.
positions.verbatim_quote: My mission has been to actively move the Gravenhurst Health Hub forward and I'm focused on initiatives that protect our environment.
positions.source_title: Candidate Profiles - Town of Gravenhurst official election page

positions.summary_short: Gordie Merton wants James Street sidewalks and the Lookout Park stairs built and funded.
summary_bullets: Will introduce an immediate motion directing staff to investigate sidewalks and multiuse pathways along James Street for the capital budget.
Will bring a motion to lock the Lookout Park stairs into the 2027 Town budget to end endless deferrals; public waterfront access must be protected.
Endorsed by the Muskoka Lakes Association.
positions.verbatim_quote: Our children and residents should never be forced to walk along narrow, snowy and unsafe road shoulders.
positions.source_title: Gordie Merton for Ward 1 Councillor | Gravenhurst - campaign website

positions.summary_short: Gordie Merton opposes overdevelopment and wants growth that respects the Official Plan and protects lake health.
summary_bullets: Stands firmly for protecting shorelines and lake health by opposing overdevelopment.
Growth must respect the Official Plan, safeguard water quality and natural ecosystems, and reflect community character.
Decisions made transparently at the local council table using municipal oversight and community input mechanisms.
positions.verbatim_quote: Growth in Gravenhurst must respect our Official Plan, safeguard water quality and natural ecosystems, and reflect the character of our community.
positions.source_title: Gordie Merton for Ward 1 Councillor | Gravenhurst - campaign website

positions.summary_short: Heidi Welker wants a vibrant year-round downtown, stronger businesses and sustainable infrastructure.
summary_bullets: Wants a vibrant year-round destination: stronger links between downtown, Muskoka Wharf and south-end business; celebrate community identity.
Supports resurgence of the BIA, attracting new businesses, expanding tourism and business events, and year-round employment.
Priorities also include streets, snow clearing, garbage collection, Health Hub improvements and attainable housing.
Environmental protection and good governance: fire prevention, supporting Muskoka Conservancy, sustainable infrastructure.
positions.verbatim_quote: I want Gravenhurst to thrive. Supporting the community and local businesses are my priorities.
positions.source_title: Candidate Profiles - Town of Gravenhurst official election page

positions.summary_short: Heidi Welker wants at least 60 beds, more beds in Bracebridge and equitable care at each site.
summary_bullets: Supports advocating for a minimum of 60 acute-care beds, citing Gravenhurst's population growth targets.
Wants more beds in Bracebridge and equitable care in each location; does not support the current MAHC model.
Says acute care is stressful enough without being moved to another hospital.
Undecided on the Pine Street site and on committing municipal funding; wants details first.
positions.verbatim_quote: We need more beds in Bracebridge and equitable care in each location.
positions.source_title: SSMHC 2026 Municipal Candidate Questionnaire Results - Gravenhurst

positions.summary_short: Elizabeth Shannon campaigns on responsible growth, a thriving economy and waterfront protection.
summary_bullets: Platform pillars: responsible and collaborative leadership; a thriving Gravenhurst; environmental stewardship and waterfront protection.
Supports responsible growth that strengthens the economy while preserving character, environment and quality of life.
Priorities: vibrant year-round downtown, economically dynamic and environmentally protected waterfront, affordable housing.
Also wants youth opportunities, arts and culture, safe sidewalks and accessibility, and meaningful relationships with Indigenous communities.
positions.verbatim_quote: Elizabeth supports responsible growth that strengthens our economy and plans for the future while preserving the character, environment, and quality of life that make Gravenhurst special.
positions.source_title: Candidate Profiles - Town of Gravenhurst official election page

positions.summary_short: Brad Rundle supports at least 60 beds and local services, and opposes funding a substandard facility.
summary_bullets: Supports a minimum of 60 acute-care beds for Muskoka's 70,000 permanent residents.
Says transporting patients takes life-saving time and money better used reinforcing South Muskoka services.
Would not commit municipal funding to what he calls a substandard and unaffordable facility.
Undecided on the current model; committed to educating himself further.
positions.verbatim_quote: Yes, I believe that we need at least this number of beds to address the needs of the 70,000 permanent residents of Muskoka.
positions.source_title: SSMHC 2026 Municipal Candidate Questionnaire Results - Gravenhurst

positions.summary_short: Erin Gauthier wants at least 60 beds and local obstetrics, and rejects the current MAHC model.
summary_bullets: Supports a minimum of 60 acute-care beds; says South Muskoka deserves equal access to proper acute care.
Losing fully functioning obstetrics would completely break her support for the model.
Would not commit municipal tax dollars to a plan that leaves South Muskoka behind.
Does not believe the proposed model is adequate or equitable.
positions.verbatim_quote: Yes, losing fully functioning obstetrical services would completely break my support for this model.
positions.source_title: SSMHC 2026 Municipal Candidate Questionnaire Results - Gravenhurst

positions.summary_short: Erin Gauthier campaigns on affordable housing, downtown revitalization and better roads.
summary_bullets: Goals: more affordable housing for full-time residents, supporting local businesses, revitalizing downtown.
Wants improved roads and infrastructure and opportunities for connection and recreation.
Former front-line crisis counsellor; brings listening without judgement and compassion.
positions.verbatim_quote: My goals are to create more affordable housing for full-time residents, support local businesses, revitalize the downtown, improve roads and infrastructure.
positions.source_title: Candidate Profiles - Town of Gravenhurst official election page

positions.summary_short: Stephen Sims wants at least 60 beds and two equivalent hospital sites, and opposes the current model.
summary_bullets: Supports a minimum of 60 acute-care beds; says South Muskoka growth requires appropriate facilities.
Wants the plan revisited for two equivalent sites; opposes municipal funding under a deal that promised two equivalent sites but did not deliver.
Does not support the current MAHC redevelopment model.
Found MAHC public meetings frustrating because the full answers never came.
positions.verbatim_quote: The Town contribution was worded in a way that expected two equivalent sites. That's not what was dropped on us.
positions.source_title: SSMHC 2026 Municipal Candidate Questionnaire Results - Gravenhurst

positions.summary_short: Stephen Sims wants responsible development that protects the lakes and opposes provincial MZOs.
summary_bullets: Goal is to see Gravenhurst prosper with responsible development that does not destroy the lakes or natural environment.
Volunteer water quality sampler for the Muskoka Lakes Association for more than 20 years.
Opposes provincially imposed MZOs: excessive proposals like Cliff Bay should not be imposed on the town.
Short-term rentals: accountability, enforcement and reasonable regulation are essential so everyone can enjoy their home.
positions.verbatim_quote: Decisions that affect Gravenhurst should be made in Gravenhurst.
positions.source_title: Stephen Sims for Ward 2 Councillor - campaign website

positions.summary_short: Stephen Sims wants fiscal restraint so budget increases match residents' incomes.
summary_bullets: Fiscal restraint: many residents face income that does not match the Town's budget increases; staff must sharpen their pencils.
Principles: protect the waterfront, protect neighbourhood character, maintain quality municipal services, keep taxes under control.
Supported road upkeep, snow clearing and garbage pickup as ongoing needs.
positions.verbatim_quote: Many in our community are facing financial hardship - with income that doesn't match the rate of the Town's budget increases.
positions.source_title: Stephen Sims for Ward 2 Councillor - campaign website

positions.summary_short: Stephen Sims wants reasonable short-term rental regulation with accountability and enforcement.
summary_bullets: Short-term rentals can benefit property owners but everyone deserves to enjoy their home without irresponsible behaviour.
Says accountability, enforcement and reasonable regulation are essential.
positions.verbatim_quote: Short term rentals can benefit property owners. But everyone deserves to enjoy their home without being subjected to irresponsible behaviour. Accountability, enforcement and reasonable regulation is essential.
positions.source_title: Stephen Sims for Ward 2 Councillor - campaign website

positions.summary_short: David Kellam wants more acute beds and local care, and supports the current MAHC redevelopment model.
summary_bullets: Supports a minimum of 60 acute-care beds for the growing and aging population.
Wants better care locally so residents do not drive long distances; supports the Pine Street site.
Says he would like obstetrics available locally, though younger families can travel.
Supports the current MAHC redevelopment model, believing it is moving in the right direction for both locations.
positions.verbatim_quote: We definitely need more acute beds to provide adequate care for our growing population and aging population.
positions.source_title: SSMHC 2026 Municipal Candidate Questionnaire Results - Gravenhurst

positions.summary_short: Carol Ann LeMoine wants at least 60 beds and says the current model inequitably concentrates beds in Huntsville.
summary_bullets: Supports a minimum of 60 acute-care beds; notes Stage 1.3 reduces South Muskoka from 65 inpatient beds to 46 while Huntsville grows.
Says all 37 reactivation and complex medical management beds would be in Huntsville under the current plan.
Notes labour and delivery moved to Huntsville in March 2025 as a temporary measure.
Does not believe the current model provides equitable access for South Muskoka.
positions.verbatim_quote: Transfers should happen because a patient needs specialized care, not because South Muskoka lacks beds or services.
positions.source_title: SSMHC 2026 Municipal Candidate Questionnaire Results - Gravenhurst

positions.summary_short: Carol Ann LeMoine prioritizes lake protection, reliable infrastructure and a year-round economy.
summary_bullets: Priorities if elected: protecting local lakes and rivers, reliable infrastructure, a thriving downtown and year-round economy.
Lifelong Morrison Lake cottager now living there year-round; executive member of the Morrison Lake Ratepayers Association with lake stewardship experience.
25 years in education as teacher, math consultant, vice-principal and principal; volunteer with Society of Saint Vincent de Paul.
positions.verbatim_quote: If elected, Carol Ann's priorities for Ward 3 include protecting local lakes and rivers, advocating for reliable infrastructure, supporting a thriving downtown and year-round economy.
positions.source_title: Candidate Profiles - Town of Gravenhurst official election page

positions.summary_short: Larry Brassard campaigns on responsible, economically sensitive taxation and community safety.
summary_bullets: Platform cornerstone: advocating for responsible, economically sensitive taxation.
Draws on his experience building corporate budgets as Fire Chief and on the Town's Senior Management Team.
Wants investment in municipal road infrastructure and community safety alongside fiscal care.
positions.verbatim_quote: Larry Brassard's municipal platform is built on four core cornerstones: advocating for responsible, economically sensitive taxation; protecting Gravenhurst's natural environment; championing housing-first supportive development; and investing heavily in local community safety and municipal road infrastructure.
positions.source_title: Vote for Larry Brassard for Ward 3 Gravenhurst Council - campaign website

positions.summary_short: Larry Brassard supports a housing-first approach with supportive housing options.
summary_bullets: Advocates a housing-first approach to local housing challenges.
Supports local municipal initiatives that bolster District-level social housing programs.
Aims for robust, supportive housing options that strengthen the community.
positions.verbatim_quote: Larry Brassard plans to address local housing challenges by advocating for a housing-first approach.
positions.source_title: Vote for Larry Brassard for Ward 3 Gravenhurst Council - campaign website

positions.summary_short: Tina Kilbourne campaigns on transparent governance, lake health, fiscal accountability and a vibrant downtown.
summary_bullets: Vision focuses on five priorities: collaborative and transparent governance; environmental stewardship and lake health; responsible growth and fiscal accountability; community health, safety and wellbeing; a vibrant downtown and strong local economy.
26 years of municipal experience in economic development, public transit, environmental stewardship and supporting vulnerable families.
Pledges evidence-based decisions with future generations in mind.
positions.verbatim_quote: My vision for Ward 5 focuses on five key priorities: Collaborative and Transparent Governance; Environmental Stewardship and Lake Health; Responsible Growth and Fiscal Accountability; Community Health, Safety and Wellbeing; A Vibrant Downtown and Strong Local Economy.
positions.source_title: Candidate Profiles - Town of Gravenhurst official election page
